title: Curve Appeal: Mike Meyers Takes Sony’s New Fisheye Lens Across Chicago
summary: Alpha Collective member Mike Meyers puts the Sony 8-14mm f/3.5 Fisheye G lens through its paces – from Wrigley Field to city streets.
body_markdown:
There are lenses that document a scene, and then there are lenses that invite photographers to rethink it. During an advance 10-day trial in Chicago,


[Alpha Collective member Mike Meyers](https://alphauniverse.com/member/#/michael-meyers) found the[Sony 8-14mm f/3.5 Fisheye G lens](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/all-e-mount/p/sel814g?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article) belongs firmly in the latter category. Meyers took the compact zoom everywhere its perspective could earn its place: a baseball game, city streets and cityscapes, a landmark cathedral, and sessions with his dog, skateboarders and rollerbladers. The result was a concentrated study in what an ultra-wide fisheye can do when it is used deliberately – not as a novelty, but as a way to bring energy, context and scale into a frame.


****


Photo by Mike Meyers. Alpha 7R V. 8-14mm f/3.5 Fisheye G. 1/320-sec. f/6.3. ISO 100.


Photo by Mike Meyers. Alpha 7R V. 8-14mm f/3.5 Fisheye G. 1/40-sec. f/3.5. ISO 100.


#### A Wider Way To See


For Meyers, the appeal begins with the focal range itself. An[8-14mm zoom](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/all-e-mount/p/sel814g?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article) lets photographers dial between a pronounced fisheye character and a broad frame that stretches subject matter from corner to corner. That flexibility changes how a photographer can approach a location.


****


Photo by Mike Meyers. Alpha 1. 8-14mm f/3.5 Fisheye G. 1/400-sec. f/3.5. ISO 100.


Photo by Mike Meyers. Alpha 1. 8-14mm f/3.5 Fisheye G. 1/100-sec. f/3.5. ISO 100.


Photo by Mike Meyers. Alpha 7R V. 8–14mm f/3.5 Fisheye G. 1/2500-sec. f/3.5. ISO 500


Photo by Mike Meyers. Alpha 7R V. 8-14mm f/3.5 Fisheye G. 1/2000-sec. f/5.6. ISO 100.


Photo by Mike Meyers. Alpha 7R V. 8–14mm f/3.5 Fisheye G. 1/1600-sec. f/3.5. ISO 200.


“You’re able to create dynamic-looking shots that you just can’t get with another lens. Also being able to fit so much of a scene into one frame lets you create images that you’d otherwise need to stitch together.”


****


Chicago provided no shortage of material. At Wrigley Field during a night game, Meyers used the lens to take in the visual density of the ballpark – its field, stands, lights and fans – in a single composition. “It’s just really cool to be able to see nearly the entire stadium in one frame. There’s so much to take in at a ballpark and to be able to have access to it all in one shot is a lot of fun.”


****


Photo by Mike Meyers. Alpha 7R V. 8-14mm f/3.5 Fisheye G. 1/80-sec. f/16. ISO 100.


Photo by Mike Meyers. Alpha 7R V. 8-14mm f/3.5 Fisheye G. 1/200-sec. f/3.5. ISO 500.


Photo by Mike Meyers. Alpha 7R V. 8–14mm f/3.5 Fisheye G. 1/40-sec. f/3.5. ISO 100.


Photo by Mike Meyers. Alpha 7R V. 8–14mm f/3.5 Fisheye G. 1/200-sec. f/4. ISO 320.


#### Small Enough To Bring Along


A specialized perspective only helps if the lens is easy enough to carry when inspiration shows up. Meyers repeatedly pointed to the[8-14mm f/3.5 Fisheye G](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/all-e-mount/p/sel814g?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article) ’s compact footprint as one of its most practical strengths. “It’s super compact – for something that’s more of a niche lens, the fact that it’s so small means you can throw it in your bag without sacrificing much space or weight, so for those times you need it, you’ve got it.”


****


That portability mattered across long walks through the city looking for fresh compositions. Meyers noted that the lens was light enough to carry for hours without fatigue, making it more approachable for spontaneous street work and exploratory shooting than a lens with such an extreme point of view might suggest.


****


Photo by Mike Meyers. Alpha 1. 8-14mm f/3.5 Fisheye G. 1/320-sec. f/3.5. ISO 1000.


Photo by Mike Meyers. Alpha 7R V. 8-14mm f/3.5 Fisheye G. 1/800-sec. f/5.6. ISO 100.


Photo by Mike Meyers. Alpha 7R V. 8-14mm f/3.5 Fisheye G. 1/1250-sec. f/6.3. ISO 100.


Photo by Mike Meyers. Alpha 1. 8-14mm f/3.5 Fisheye G. 1/200-sec. f/3.5. ISO 100.


#### Built For Motion & Sharpness


The lens also had to keep up when the scene moved. Meyers tested autofocus with skateboarders and rollerbladers in action, where timing and focus accuracy are essential.


Photo by Mike Meyers. Alpha 1. 8-14mm f/3.5 Fisheye G. 1/500-sec. f/3.5. ISO 500.


Photo by Mike Meyers. Alpha 1. 8-14mm f/3.5 Fisheye G. 1/1000-sec. f/10. ISO 500.


“I thought AF was super fast and on target – I was able to get shots of skateboarders and rollerbladers doing tricks and I don’t think it missed focus once.”


****


The combination of responsive autofocus, compact size and sharp rendering made the lens feel capable beyond static architecture or intentional distortion. Meyers’ favorite qualities came back to the lens’ visual signature and its execution. “Just the overall look it gives you, and the fact that it’s sharp and compact. I really loved how small the lens was and how easy it was to carry for hours at a time when I was out looking for comps.”


Photo by Mike Meyers. Alpha 1. 8–14mm f/3.5 Fisheye G. 1/250-sec. f/3.5. ISO 100.


Photo by Mike Meyers. Alpha 1. 8-14mm f/3.5 Fisheye G. 1/20-sec. f/3.5. ISO 1000.


#### A Specialist Tool With Real Creative Upside


****


For Meyers, the[8-14mm f/3.5 Fisheye G](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/all-e-mount/p/sel814g?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article) is not necessarily an everyday replacement for the workhorse lenses already in his kit. He regularly carries a 12-24mm, 24-70mm, 70-200mm and 100-400mm, along with two bodies. Still, he sees a clear role for this lens when a scene calls for heightened scale, movement or immersion. “In certain instances, this would be the lens you’d want to have for a super dynamic shot.”


****


Photo by Mike Meyers. Alpha 7R V. 8–14mm f/3.5 Fisheye G. 1/1600-sec. f/5.6. ISO 100.


Photo by Mike Meyers. Alpha 7R V. 8-14mm f/3.5 Fisheye G. 1/80-sec. f/3.5. ISO 320.


Photo by Mike Meyers. Alpha 7R V. 8-14mm f/3.5 Fisheye G. 1/1250-sec. f/8. ISO 100.


That is exactly where the[8-14mm f/3.5 Fisheye G](https://electronics.sony.com/imaging/lenses/all-e-mount/p/sel814g?utm_source=AlphaUniverse&utm_medium=Web&utm_campaign=Article) makes its case: not as a lens for every scene, but as a compact creative option that can transform the right one. From the charged atmosphere of Wrigley Field to fast-moving skaters and the geometry of Chicago’s urban landscape, Meyers found a lens designed to pull viewers into the center of the action.


****


Photo by Mike Meyers. Alpha 7R V. 8–14mm f/3.5 Fisheye G. 1/800-sec. f/5.6. ISO 100.


“If you’re looking to try something new and mix up the look of your shots, or need some really dynamic B-roll, definitely check this lens out.”


****
